text:
New Victor Moses? How Alonso has transformed Neto
- Published
Just as they did 10 years ago, Chelsea are thriving after moving a winger into a wing-back role, with Pedro Neto the latest player to benefit.
A decade ago, it was Victor Moses who made the switch, adapting to Antonio Conte's then-innovative system and helping Chelsea to a 13-match winning run en route to the Premier League title in 2017.
Neto scored twice from wing-back in Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday.
However, the situation could have unfolded very differently for the 26-year-old.
Chelsea did not regard the Portuguese as untouchable during the summer, although they had set a lofty asking price of about £100m.
They knew Neto was among the players frustrated at the end of last season after Enzo Maresca, with whom he had a close relationship, left the club on New Year's Day. His managerial successor, Liam Rosenior, lasted less than four months in charge as Chelsea finished 10th.
At the end of last season and throughout the summer, players including Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Reece James and Moises Caicedo signed new contracts after buying into Chelsea's revised vision of adding experience alongside the talent already assembled.
The appointment of Xabi Alonso also appeared to win players over, although there were questions about whether Neto relished the prospect of playing at wing-back, and uncertainty over his future persisted until the transfer window closed.
Yet last month, Neto signed a new contract until 2032 after emerging as a key player under Alonso.
Like several team-mates, he has since publicly backed Chelsea's project under Alonso.
Chelsea are getting the best of both worlds
Perhaps Alonso saw something in Neto that the player did not initially see in himself.
Despite joining Chelsea from Wolves for £54m in 2024, the attacker had never been particularly prolific, scoring 14 goals and providing 27 assists in 135 appearances for the Midlands club.
His output improved only marginally at Stamford Bridge before Alonso's arrival, with 19 goals and 19 assists in 103 appearances.
Since then, however, he has scored four goals and provided one assist in nine appearances this season, despite three of those coming as a substitute. That is more than double the strike-rate he had achieved previously.
Indeed, Chelsea are now getting the best of both worlds.
Despite operating as a wing-back, he is averaging 5.3 touches in the opposition box per 90 minutes compared with 3.6 last season.
His successful dribbles have risen from 1.6 to 1.8 per 90 minutes, while his dribble success rate has increased from 43.5% to 52.6%. He is also creating more chances, with his average climbing from 1.8 to 2.0 per 90, including an increase in open-play chances created from 1.5 to 1.8.
His defensive responsibilities have also increased significantly, with tackles rising from 0.7 to 2.0 per 90 and possessions won increasing from 2.9 to 3.9, all in the Premier League.
It owes to Neto's athleticism, which he has previously attributed in part to growing up in a family of roller-hockey players, allowing him to impact both ends of the pitch.
In Chelsea's finest hour under the current American ownership, Neto effectively man-marked Achraf Hakimi as Chelsea beat Paris St-Germain 3-0 in the Club World Cup final in 2025.
On Saturday, Alonso said of Neto's position: "You can call him whatever you want. Winger, wing-back, attacking player, defensive player. He can do many things.
"Today he did well. He is very competitive and whenever he is close to the action he is a threat against any full-back."
It is an asymmetric approach from Alonso, who does not demand the same attacking output from his left-sided wing-back, usually Jorrel Hato or Pep Chavarria. That gives Neto greater licence to drive forward on the opposite flank.
In addition, Alonso will appreciate his status as a dressing room joker among his team-mates.
His former Wolves team-mate Conor Coady was working as a pundit for Sky Sports after Chelsea's 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds, in which Neto scored, and asked him: "When have you ever been worried about conceding goals?"
Neto replied: "Now I am a wing-back, lad."
The response prompted laughter from both men before Neto added: "In my head, I always have to run back and help my defenders as well."
A decade ago, Moses transformed himself under Conte to great effect. Neto has not had to change quite as much. Instead, his switch from winger to right wing-back under Alonso has amplified the qualities that were already there.
digest_he:
צ'לסי מוצאת את עצמה שוב נהנית מהסבה מוצלחת של שחקן קו לתפקיד כנף-הגנה, כפי שעשתה לפני עשר שנים עם ויקטור מוזס תחת אנטוניו קונטה. הפעם זהו פדרו נטו הפורטוגלי שפורח בתפקיד החדש תחת הדרכתו של המאמן צ'אבי אלונסו, ואף כבש צמד ניצחון מול אברטון.

ההצלחה הנוכחית מגיעה לאחר תקופה לא פשוטה עבור השחקן בן ה-26, ששמו נקשר בעבר בעזיבה והתלבט לנוכח חוסר היציבות בניהול המקצועי של המועדון. אולם, לאחר מינויו של אלונסו והארכת חוזהו עד שנת 2032, הפך נטו לשחקן מפתח בקבוצה וממלא שתי משימות במגרש ביעילות רבה.

הנתונים הסטטיסטיים מצביעים על זינוק ניכר ביכולתו: הוא מעורב יותר באזורים המסוכנים ברחבת היריב, יוצר מצבים רבים יותר לחבריו, ומפגין מעורבות הגנתית עמוקה הכוללת תיקולים וחטיפות כדור בהיקפים גבוהים בהרבה מבעבר. יכולותיו האתלטיות והמחויבות הקבוצתית הפכו אותו לנשק טקטי משמעותי במערך של צ'לסי.
